title: Making Urine More Concentrated Than Blood

scenes.visual: Title card 'Making Urine More Concentrated Than Blood' over a vertical slice of a cartoon kidney. Same COLOUR MAP as the first film: blood RED; filtrate and urine YELLOW (amber); salt ORANGE dots; urea small GREY dots; water BLUE drops; tissue concentration a light-to-dark ORANGE shading (more concentrated = darker). Antidiuretic hormone is always the same GOLD KEY icon. All drawings are schematic cartoons labelled 'schematic'.

scenes.tts: The first film showed the kidney taking back almost all filtered water. The last litres are the hardest.
scenes.visual: The first film's left-to-right nephron with its ledger bar shrinks to a corner thumbnail. The thin YELLOW exit stream is circled, label 'the last litres'.
scenes.narration: The first film showed the kidney taking back almost all filtered water. The last litres are the hardest.

scenes.tts: A water-deprived adult can make urine about four times as concentrated as plasma. Yet no pump in the kidney moves water. So how does it pull water out of such urine?
scenes.visual: Two beakers: 'plasma, about 290 mOsm per kg' with a few ORANGE dots, and 'most concentrated human urine, near 1,200' crowded with ORANGE dots. A pump icon labelled 'water pump' appears and is crossed out. Question mark.
scenes.narration: A water-deprived adult can make urine about four times as concentrated as plasma. Yet no pump in the kidney moves water. So how does it pull water out of such urine?

scenes.tts: Concentration here means osmolality, the number of dissolved particles in each kilogram of water. Water moves by osmosis, toward the more concentrated side. So the tissue outside must be a little more concentrated than the urine. Salt supplies most, and deep down, urea helps.
scenes.visual: Label 'osmolality = dissolved particles per kg of water'. A membrane splits a box: left side few particles, right side many ORANGE dots and a few GREY urea dots. BLUE drops drift across to the crowded side. Then the box becomes a tube (YELLOW urine inside) in ORANGE-shaded tissue; BLUE drops leave the tube only once the tissue shading is a little darker than the tube. Small labels 'salt' and 'urea (deep medulla)'.
scenes.narration: Concentration here means osmolality, the number of dissolved particles in each kilogram of water. Water moves by osmosis, toward the more concentrated side. So the tissue outside must be a little more concentrated than the urine. Salt supplies most, and deep down, urea helps.

scenes.tts: Picture a slice of kidney. The outer layer is the cortex. Beneath lies the medulla, an outer zone above an inner zone. It ends at the papilla, where urine drains. A hairpin tube, the loop of Henle, dips into it.
scenes.visual: A vertical slab: top band 'cortex', then 'outer medulla', then 'inner medulla' tapering to 'papilla' with a YELLOW drip leaving. The medulla starts unshaded. A hairpin tube draws itself down from the cortex deep into the inner medulla and back up, label 'loop of Henle'. A straight tube beside it, faint for now, label 'collecting duct'.
scenes.narration: Picture a slice of kidney. The outer layer is the cortex. Beneath lies the medulla, an outer zone above an inner zone. It ends at the papilla, where urine drains. A hairpin tube, the loop of Henle, dips into it.

scenes.tts: Start with the loop's upward arm. In the outer medulla it is thick, the thick ascending limb. It moves salt out, but its wall lets almost no water through. Salt leaves, water stays, and the tissue gets saltier.
scenes.visual: The upward arm is thin in the inner medulla (label 'thin ascending limb') and thickens only where it enters the outer medulla, solid wall, label 'thick ascending limb'. ORANGE dots step out through the thick wall into the outer-medulla tissue only; BLUE drops inside bump the wall and stay. The outer-medulla tissue beside it shades one step darker ORANGE. The fluid inside the thick arm pales.
scenes.narration: Start with the loop's upward arm. In the outer medulla it is thick, the thick ascending limb. It moves salt out, but its wall lets almost no water through. Salt leaves, water stays, and the tissue gets saltier.

scenes.tts: Now the thin descending limb, the downward arm. In rabbit tubules, it lets water through but holds its salt. Passing salty tissue, it loses water by osmosis, so its fluid concentrates on the way down.
scenes.visual: The downward arm is drawn thin with open pores, label 'thin descending limb (rabbit)'. As YELLOW fluid flows down past the darker tissue, BLUE drops leave through the pores; ORANGE dots stay inside, and the fluid's own shading darkens as it descends.
scenes.narration: Now the thin descending limb, the downward arm. In rabbit tubules, it lets water through but holds its salt. Passing salty tissue, it loses water by osmosis, so its fluid concentrates on the way down.

scenes.tts: The two arms carry fluid in opposite directions. Concentrated fluid rounds the bend, so the ascending limb works from a saltier start. Level by level, a modest difference adds up. This is the countercurrent multiplier. Deeper down, how the rise continues is still debated.
scenes.visual: Arrows: down in the left arm, up in the right arm, label 'countercurrent flow'. Dark fluid rounds the bend; ORANGE dots step out of the thick ascending limb, level by level through the outer medulla; the outer-medulla shading deepens in a looping animation, label 'countercurrent multiplier'. The inner medulla shades darker still toward the papilla, with a small '?' label 'inner medulla: mechanism debated'. No numbers.
scenes.narration: The two arms carry fluid in opposite directions. Concentrated fluid rounds the bend, so the ascending limb works from a saltier start. Level by level, a modest difference adds up. This is the countercurrent multiplier. Deeper down, how the rise continues is still debated.

scenes.tts: Suppose the thick ascending limb let water through as easily as the descending limb. Would the multiplier still work well? Pause and decide.
scenes.visual: The thick ascending limb's solid wall flickers to an open, pored wall. The band freezes. Two answer cards: 'still works well' and 'badly weakened'.
scenes.narration: Suppose the thick ascending limb let water through as easily as the descending limb. Would the multiplier still work well? Pause and decide.

scenes.visual: Predict pause. Cards hold. A 5-second ring timer at bottom right.

scenes.tts: Badly weakened. Water would follow the salt out, and most of the difference across the wall would collapse. Salt moving without water is the trick.
scenes.visual: With the leaky wall, each ORANGE dot that steps out is followed by BLUE drops; the shading band fades most of the way back toward pale. Card 'badly weakened' lights. The wall snaps back to solid and the band returns. Caption on screen: 'salt without water'.
scenes.narration: Badly weakened. Water would follow the salt out, and most of the difference across the wall would collapse. Salt moving without water is the trick.

scenes.tts: Is real tissue graded like this? Wirz, Hargitay and Kuhn measured the freezing point of thin rat kidney slices from different depths. More particles mean a lower freezing point. Osmolality rose from cortex toward papilla.
scenes.visual: A cartoon rat kidney is cut into thin horizontal slices from cortex to papilla; each slice drops onto a cartoon thermometer. Freezing points step lower for deeper slices. A schematic rising line, label 'osmolality, schematic', climbs from cortex to papilla beside the shaded slab. Label 'rat, 1951'.
scenes.narration: Is real tissue graded like this? Wirz, Hargitay and Kuhn measured the freezing point of thin rat kidney slices from different depths. More particles mean a lower freezing point. Osmolality rose from cortex toward papilla.

scenes.tts: The collecting duct runs from cortex to papilla through ever more concentrated tissue. Antidiuretic hormone, A D H, acts on its cells. They insert stored water channels, aquaporin two, facing the urine.
scenes.caption: The collecting duct runs from cortex to papilla through ever more concentrated tissue. Antidiuretic hormone, ADH, acts on its cells. They insert stored water channels, aquaporin-2, facing the urine.
scenes.visual: The collecting duct brightens beside the loop, YELLOW urine flowing down it. The GOLD KEY (label 'ADH') arrives; inside the duct cells, small door-shaped channels (label 'aquaporin-2') slide from vesicles into the wall facing the urine.
scenes.narration: The collecting duct runs from cortex to papilla through ever more concentrated tissue. Antidiuretic hormone, ADH, acts on its cells. They insert stored water channels, aquaporin-2, facing the urine.

scenes.tts: Water leaves the urine by osmosis into the concentrated medulla. The urine comes out concentrated. Take A D H away, the channels withdraw, and dilute urine flows out.
scenes.caption: Water leaves the urine by osmosis into the concentrated medulla. The urine comes out concentrated. Take ADH away, the channels withdraw, and dilute urine flows out.
scenes.visual: BLUE drops leave the duct through the doors into the dark tissue at every depth; the urine at the papilla darkens to deep YELLOW, label 'concentrated'. The GOLD KEY lifts away; the doors slide back into vesicles; pale YELLOW urine flows out, label 'dilute'.
scenes.narration: Water leaves the urine by osmosis into the concentrated medulla. The urine comes out concentrated. Take ADH away, the channels withdraw, and dilute urine flows out.

scenes.tts: So the kidney never pumps water. It moves solute first, building a medulla more concentrated than blood. Water follows where A D H opens the way.
scenes.caption: So the kidney never pumps water. It moves solute first, building a medulla more concentrated than blood. Water follows where ADH opens the way.
scenes.visual: The whole slab in one frame: ORANGE dots leaving the thick ascending limb in the outer medulla, GREY urea dots in the inner medulla, the shaded band, BLUE drops leaving the collecting duct with the GOLD KEY in place. The first film's ledger bar appears at top with 'reabsorbed (water)' glowing.
scenes.narration: So the kidney never pumps water. It moves solute first, building a medulla more concentrated than blood. Water follows where ADH opens the way.

scenes.visual: Hex end card. Line: 'No pump moves water: move solute first, and water follows.'
